subject: Post-demo: latency & streaming SLA qualification — next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — latency / streaming questions and proposed next steps

Tom — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance qualification for your payments fraud pipeline.

Key items we heard from your side:
- Target: p95 end-to-end latency of <= 350ms for short prompt flows (<= 512 tokens) and p95 <= 700ms for typical 2-3k token context windows.
- Throughput/concurrency: sustained 250 QPS with bursts to 1k QPS during batch processing windows; typical concurrency per worker is 40 streams.
- Streaming: you rely on response-start latency (time-to-first-token) for UX; incremental token delivery matters for the fraud analyst UI.
- Measurement: you want latency measured in production (e2e) and exposed via a weekly report.

Questions we promised to follow up on during the call:
1) How we define "latency" in the SLA: start-of-response vs. full-response vs. per-token tail.
2) Exclusions: large-context long-running requests, scheduled maintenance, and customer-supplied heavy preprocessing.
3) Remedies/credits and monitoring cadence you expect for violations.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- We will run a focused perf validation: a 48-hour load test using your sample prompt set (we requested the sample set; thanks Lara for sending the initial file).
- We'll provide two candidate SLA wording options: one focused on response-start SLOs (for streaming UX) and one focused on full-response SLOs (for total latency-sensitive pipelines).
- Tentative timeline: perf run by COB Wed (48h), draft SLA by Thu morning, sync call Fri to review.

Attachments: fintechco_perf_requirements.xlsx (xlsx) — your sample load patterns; redwood_latency_streaming_sla_draft.docx (docx) — initial language (first draft incoming).

Thanks — I looped Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (solutions/infrastructure) to help with the perf plan and contractual language.

—
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mailto:aisha_rahman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@fintechco.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Nguyen <lara.nguyen@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — latency / streaming questions and proposed next steps

Aisha — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Preference is definitely on response-start (time-to-first-token) for the analyst UI; that metric most directly maps to perceived snappiness. For batch fraud scoring, full-response latency is more relevant. We'll need both measured.
- For the streaming UX, p50 start should be <= 120ms, p95 start <= 300ms. For full-response, your suggested 350/700 p95s sound reasonable but we may push for a 500ms p95 for the 2–3k workflows if the perf tests justify it.
- Exclusions: requests over 8k token context, requests using synchronous external lookups during request processing, and scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notice.
- Remedies: we prefer financial credits for repeated breaches, but are open to a combination of credits + escalation SLA (weekend escalation window).

We can proceed with the perf harness you proposed. Lara will share the sample prompt set and the synthetic traffic profile this afternoon.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Blake
VP Product, FinTechCo

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Draft SLA language & perf plan — internal review before sending to FinTechCo

Team — drafting options for the SLA language and the perf validation checklist. Leaving notes inline so we can finalize before sending to Tom/Lara.

Notes / proposed clauses:
A) Definitions
- "Response-start latency": time from Redwood's receipt of a canonical request (post-auth/rate-limit) to the first application token emitted from the model (server-side time), measured at the edge and aggregated to p50/p95/p99.
- "Full-response latency": time from Redwood's receipt of request to final token emitted and flushed to the client.
- "Concurrent stream": an open streaming connection counted per active request.

B) SLO candidates (customer-facing, pick one or both):
1) Streaming-first SLO (UX focused): p95 response-start <= 300ms for requests <= 512 tokens; p50 <= 120ms. Scope: production traffic routed to Redwood's hosted cluster in us-west-2, sustained load up to 250 QPS; bursts up to 1k QPS tolerated for up to 10 minutes.
2) Full-response SLO (throughput focused): p95 full-response <= 700ms for requests with context <= 3k tokens under sustained load of 250 QPS.

C) Exclusions (examples to include explicitly):
- Scheduled maintenance windows with 48h prior notice.
- Customer-induced delays: long pre-processing hooks, external sync calls that block request completion.
- Requests exceeding the agreed-upon context length (8k tokens) or using unsupported model variants.
- Third-party cloud network outages (defined by provider status page).

D) Measurement & Reporting
- Measurement point: edge ingress (closest Redwood edge) for e2e measurement; we will provide both server-side and client-observed latency histograms.
- Reporting cadence: weekly aggregated report (token counts, p50/p95/p99 for response-start and full-response), monthly SLA summary with rolling 30-day windows.
- Alerting: automated paged alerts if p95 response-start breaches threshold for >15 minutes.

E) Remedies
- Tiered credit schedule: single-day violation credit of 10% of daily consumption for first breach; recurring breaches over a rolling 30-day window escalate to 25% credits and a mandatory architecture review.
- Immediate operational remedy: priority escalation path to Redwood SREs within 2 hours of a confirmed incident during business hours; weekend support available under enterprise plan.

F) Perf validation plan (what we run next)
- 48-hour ramped soak: synthetic traffic matching FinTechCo profile (250 QPS sustained, 1k QPS bursts), mixture of short (<=512 tokens) and long (2–3k tokens) contexts, streaming and non-streaming calls.
- Measure response-start and full-response both client-observed and server-side.
- Provide raw histograms, sample traces, and a regression checklist (KV cache warm, model variant pinned).

Action items before external send:
- Marissa: confirm credits language is acceptable from commercial (I recall we typically cap credits at X% — please confirm).
- Aisha: coordinate perf run and collect FinTechCo prompt set (Lara).
- Karthik: produce two short SLA text options (streaming-first, full-response-first) and attach to the outbound.

Attachment stub: redwood_latency_streaming_sla_draft.docx (we will finalize after Marissa review).

—
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lara Nguyen <lara_nguyen@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: SLA wording proposals + next steps (perf run scheduled)

Tom / Lara — thanks for the quick responses and for sharing the prompt set, Lara. We scheduled the 48-hour perf validation to start tonight at 22:00 PDT against a staging cluster that mirrors our us-west-2 hosted profile. Key things to expect:

1) Deliverables by Thu 09:00 PDT
- Two short SLA language options (attached): "Streaming-first SLO" and "Full-response SLO". Each is ~3 paragraphs and includes measurement point and common exclusions.
- Perf run summary draft with p50/p95/p99 histograms for both response-start and full-response.

2) Quick clarifications requested before the run (Lara, please confirm):
- Are sample prompt tokens trimmed to remove PII? We will not include plaintext production PII in the shared synthetic tests.
- Confirm burst behavior tolerance: you asked that 1k QPS bursts be tolerated for up to 10 minutes — confirm whether bursts can be any time of day or only during the nightly batch window.

3) Proposed mutual action plan (MAP)
- Tonight: kick perf run (Redwood).
- Thu morning: Redwood shares raw histograms + draft SLA wording.
- Thu afternoon: 30m sync to pick SLA option and negotiate credits/escape clauses.
- Fri: finalize contract language and route to procurement.

Attachment references: redwood_latency_streaming_sla_draft.docx (docx) — contains the two candidate sections; fintechco_perf_requirements.xlsx (xlsx) — your traffic profile.

If the streaming-first option aligns best with your UX needs, we'll recommend pairing it with a negotiated burst policy and a 30-day rolling measurement window. If you prefer credits limits to be firmer, flag that now and Marissa will run the commercial check.

Looking forward — Aisha
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
